brief: Asia chopped as AI-driven selloff concerns linger. KOSPI and Samsung/Hynix partially retraced yesterday's 5.5% drop after ASML's blowout numbers raised the low end of 2026 guidance and flagged demand extending into 2029/30, implying it lacks capacity to meet customers, but the absence of a 2027 estimate upgrade left the market wanting a bigger upward reset. On rates, Fed's Williams signaled the Fed wants to hold in October unless forced, with today's CPI (consensus 0.6% headline, 0.2% core) the key test. Bonds have rallied and rate vol has compressed as financial tightening reverses, against one-sided positioning and a resilient ex-AI consumer. In energy, heating oil threatens new highs on an unresolved distillate shortage, and European gas (TTF) hit new highs near 86, adding to inflation and economic strain. Saudi escalation against the Houthis raises risk to energy infrastructure. On AI, frontier competition (Google's Gemini 4 Argon, Anthropic's investor event) keeps demand accelerating, but CCC credit spreads have widened over 200bp since September as financing AI capex through 2028 alongside huge sovereign deficits raises the cost of capital, which the author argues, not demand, is now the binding constraint on AI spending, with hyperscalers favored to own the scarcity.
